Peter, Winning the next election isn’t enough. We need to give the American people a vision for the future—and be ready on day one to govern with a mandate that puts workers and families first. Hi Peter, Eva Longoria here.
We are officially 38 days away from Election Day, and there are a lot of critical races on the ballot this fall. But the Texas governor’s race is especially important and personal to me, and my friend Gina Hinojosa needs your support right now.
I’ll tell you why I’m so proud to stand with Gina in just a moment, but first: [**Will you make a donation of any amount today to power her campaign for Governor of Texas?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260926_4_eva.ER3Iee&refcode=em20260926-2243&amount=5&t=2&akid=2243%2E299639%2ETtYQv6)
Like Gina, I was born and raised in South Texas. I am a proud Texan through and through. **But the Texas that Gina and I grew up in is simply not the Texas our families are living in today.**
We were raised on the American Dream. The core belief that if you work hard, you can buy a home, raise a family, build a career, and live with security. But under Greg Abbott's leadership, that promise has been stripped away.
Because of Greg Abbott, everyday families are stuck paying more and getting less. From his no-bid contracts to his public school voucher scam and massive corporate tax giveaways for his ultra-wealthy friends, hard-working Texans are the ones stuck paying the bill.
**Texans deserve better. We pay for strong public schools, reliable infrastructure, and lower costs, and it is time we actually get what we deserve.** And I know that if we elect Gina this fall, we can make Texas a state where everyone can prosper.
This November, we have a real opportunity to win a better Texas and restore the American Dream for every family. But Gina can’t take on Greg Abbott without our collective support right now.
**[Peter, will you join me and pitch in any amount to Gina’s campaign today to finally bring real, honest leadership back to Texas?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260926_4_eva.ER3Iee&refcode=em20260926-2243&amount=5&t=3&akid=2243%2E299639%2ETtYQv6)**

Thank you for being a part of this fight for a better Texas.
— Eva Longoria

That’s why I’m asking you to support Jon Ossoff’s reelection campaign today. I’ll explain more in just a moment, but first, [**can you chip in $5 — or whatever you’re able — to help defend Jon’s seat?**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-sep26.MEWcSy&refcode=em260926-4-f&utm_campaign=em260926-4-f&t=3&akid=2942%2E5691347%2ER9tQkX) _Donald Trump and his extremist allies in Congress are wreaking havoc on our nation’s most vital institutions and engaging in corruption on a level this nation has never seen before._ Pillars of our democracy — like the rule of law, a free press, and the ability to voice dissent openly — are being blatantly targeted by this administration’s top officials, all while Trump caters to the billionaire class. Republicans in Congress have the power to put a stop to this. It would take only a handful to vote with the Democrats and say that Donald Trump has to follow the law. But it seems like the Republicans in Congress have all had their spines removed. # New Mexico voters aren't a sideshow
---
| | | | | | Friend,
Deb Haaland has turned down a debate with every major news outlet in New Mexico.
KRQE offered a debate. KOAT offered a debate. KVIA offered a debate. The Albuquerque Journal and the Santa Fe New Mexican each offered a debate. I said yes to every single one. She said no to every single one.
This week, she walked away from KOB too, the one debate her own campaign had agreed to. Her campaign's explanation? They said they want to "move past this sideshow."
Think about that. A debate is the one night when both candidates stand on the same stage, with no script and no handlers, and answer directly to the people of New Mexico. That is what Deb Haaland's campaign is calling a sideshow.
This mess was of her campaign's own making. I agreed to the KOB debate on June 3, the day after the primary. Her campaign waited until July 20 to agree. When KOB picked October 8 as a compromise between both campaigns, she said she couldn't make it. Every date she offered instead falls after early voting begins on October 6.
That isn't a scheduling problem. It's a strategy: keep voters from seeing her on a debate stage until they've already started casting ballots.
**New Mexico voters aren't a sideshow.** They're the whole point. They deserve to see both candidates answer tough questions, side by side, before a single ballot is cast. If **Deb Haaland thinks answering to them is beneath her** , that tells you exactly how she would govern.
**I'll be at KOB on October 8 at 6 p.m., just like I said I would.** There will be two podiums on that stage. Whether she fills hers is up to her.
If she won't face voters on a debate stage, you know she’ll fill the airwaves with attack ads using her out of state money. So I'll have to make sure voters hear from me everywhere else: on TV, in their mailboxes, and on their phones in every corner of this state before early voting opens. That's less than two weeks away, and I intend to make every day count. Will you chip in $25, $50, or $100 right now to help me reach every voter before October 6?

name: Chris Pappas
subject: A gold mind in Azerbaijan
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9159%2E582294%2End6DXA ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9159%2E582294%2End6DXA ]Chris Pappas for Senate

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260927_1.rTuYlT&refcode=em20260927-9159&amount=5&t=1003&akid=9159%2E582294%2End6DXA ][IMG]
Josh Rogers/NHPR

At the GOP debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he's running
for Senate to send me back to "bussing tables” at my family’s “chicken
restaurant."

He meant it as an insult. As if the people who work in restaurants — who
cook your food, clear your plates, keep family businesses that are the
heart of our state alive — have something to be embarrassed about.

I’m not embarrassed. I’m proud.

My family opened our restaurant over 100 years ago. I know what a 65-hour
week feels like because I've worked one. I know what it means to show up
every day, work hard, and treat the people around you like they matter —
because they do.

John Sununu has never had to work hard a day in his life. He was born into
the Sununu political dynasty. His family's "business" isn't a restaurant
serving New Hampshire families. It owns a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan
that sells minerals to China.

That's what John Sununu calls “honest work.”

New Hampshire workers deserve a senator who knows what a hard day's labor
actually looks like — who fights for small business owners, for restaurant
workers, for every family just trying to make ends meet. John Sununu is
running to protect people like himself. I'm running for everyone else.

He showed us who he is with these elitist comments. Now let’s make sure he
doesn’t represent us.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260927_1.rTuYlT&amount=5&refcode=em20260927-1&t=1022&akid=9159%2E582294%2End6DXA ]Donate $5 »

John Sununu doesn’t know the real New Hampshire. He doesn’t get how hard
we work — and he sure as hell doesn’t think our labor is worth respecting.

I do. That’s why I’m running for Senate.

— Chris Pappas

Derek, **Right now, we know what you’re probably thinking:_“Great, another email asking for money.”_** We know there’s a big fundraising deadline around the corner, and that your inbox is probably flooded with candidates and organizations asking for a few dollars. But we’d like to explain how your $7 goes the furthest when given to the DNC. **We’ll keep it brief, we promise.** The FEC’s last end-of-quarter fundraising deadline before Election Day is this Wednesday (September 30), and we set a goal of raising $1 million to make sure we can afford to keep our midterm game plan running. Peter, you’ve
probably seen countless stories about artificial intelligence dominating
the news or your social media feeds recently.

While tech executives talk about how this technology could end humanity, a
reality is unfolding that has gone underdiscussed: following in the
footsteps of AIPAC and the Israel lobby, AI companies are actively trying
to buy our democracy.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260927-1.gwYZ3k&refcode=em20260927-38297&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=38297%2E1203867%2E2P6Dn8 ]Politico: AI and crypto groups were among the biggest players in this

“spent a whopping $127 million across more than 100 primaries this year in
an effort to shape the future of Congress — and won roughly 90 percent of
them.” Their influence is so strong that at least 1 in 6 members of the
incoming Congress was backed by them.

We’ve already seen the impact of their spending. An Anthropic-backed PAC
spent $1.6 million against Justice Democrat Nida Allam in the NC-04
primary. She lost by just 1% — and that kind of money could have been the
difference-maker.

If we’re going to fill Congress with leaders who answer to the working

name: Public Land Warriors
subject: The eviction of the American bison
body:
This. Is. Wrong.
This. Is. Wrong.

| [|
---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/KmXAoBPunNisc75JIwLMJg~~/AAUS1hA~/JL5XNCOzMwgzGNo1Q-GM6pOz6PseErs3ueIT3ttc8BmrnJrYrG81sfaLACfqCsr4q1VHSs5ssevdICzU18svgHIECw0DDkCtJj_Kx0UZxEVwF4z1JnTSXjHzSlRmw9Z2)
| | | | Peter, For decades, bison have legally grazed on federal grasslands in Montana. But this winter, the Bureau of Land Management **suddenly reversed course, tore up the permits, and issued a formal eviction notice to nearly 1,000 bison on the prairie.** The administration suddenly decided that bison no longer count as "livestock" under the Taylor Grazing Act because they aren't being raised for "production-oriented purposes." Because this specific herd is managed for conservation and ecosystem health rather than maximum commercial slaughter, the government declared them ineligible to eat the grass. They want the bison hauled off so 63,000 acres of your public land can be handed over exclusively to commercial cattle operations. Here is why this matters to every single person who cares about the outdoors:
* This is a calculated move to establish that public lands exist _solely_ for private profit and corporate extraction.
* If they can arbitrarily ban the American bison—the literal, snorting symbol of the American West—from the prairie using a bureaucratic loophole, they can eliminate anything that stands in the way of a commercial lease.
* This policy shift was spearheaded by political appointees who were granted special ethics waivers to shape federal policy that directly benefits their former cattle industry clients.

clean_body: This. Is. Wrong. This. Is. Wrong. | | | | | Peter, For decades, bison have legally grazed on federal grasslands in Montana. But this winter, the Bureau of Land Management suddenly reversed course, tore up the permits, and issued a formal eviction notice to nearly 1,000 bison on the prairie. The administration suddenly decided that bison no longer count as "livestock" under the Taylor Grazing Act because they aren't being raised for "production-oriented purposes." Because this specific herd is managed for conservation and ecosystem health rather than maximum commercial slaughter, the government declared them ineligible to eat the grass. They want the bison hauled off so 63,000 acres of your public land can be handed over exclusively to commercial cattle operations. Here is why this matters to every single person who cares about the outdoors: This is a calculated move to establish that public lands exist solely for private profit and corporate extraction. If they can arbitrarily ban the American bison—the literal, snorting symbol of the American West—from the prairie using a bureaucratic loophole, they can eliminate anything that stands in the way of a commercial lease. This policy shift was spearheaded by political appointees who were granted special ethics waivers to shape federal policy that directly benefits their former cattle industry clients. We are not going to let them turn our prairies into a privatized feedlot. They think they can quietly evict the bison to appease their donors. #

🚨 Friends, please don’t click away: This is a message for everybody who cares about our movement for gun safety. 👋
Donald Trump’s administration is trying to change the rules to let the USPS deliver guns through the mail — with no background checks, licensing, or training — and we need your support to fight back.

Since 1927, federal law has barred the United States Postal Service from carrying or delivering handguns as mail — with exceptions for members of the military, law enforcement, or licensed gun manufacturers or dealers.
Donald Trump is trying to change that:
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260927-1-b&t=1&akid=11860%2E3935704%2ETdAwi3)
His Department of Justice recently issued a memo saying that they would no longer enforce this ban. Now, the USPS is proposing a change to their existing regulations.

If this rule goes into effect, it would mean people who shouldn’t have a gun will be able to go around state and federal laws and get a gun mailed to them.
**This change also means that gun traffickers have a new way to move firearms through America’s communities.**
At a time when gun violence is the #1 killer of kids and teenagers in our country...this rule would make us all less safe. We need to fight back.

You have helped us so much fighting back against extremist legislation and passing gun safety laws. Now, we need your support again to push back on this proposed rule.

body:

---
| | | | | [View in browser](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMTJ9AAwAAAAAAy-YEiIyuTsUmYoe6ket6RH9ojXfhNd5JFxbbt-Nwa80BumyYZ_ewQF1zPwEnYwEbw5njAMwJwFzW1UEBmxkkPF-bbV5KUZ-KFnkh4Pylw "View in Browser")
---
_**A Special Message from our Sponsor**_ _Please note that views expressed in this message do not necessarily reflect those of_ _Free Speech Daily_ _and do not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by Free Speech Daily_ _._
---
| John Fetterman lies, half-truths, innuendos, and smears... | | | | | [](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMTJ9AAwAAAAAAy-YEiIzywGDgupzBZtO3FpehYFvI1Le5vkM02oWXWtMTkTztkWx_CR8b13a9Ijcuq3KdK7EHlnTtqnSqNO8kQBqQWTUnTeAiY6SMcc9mw)
---
| | Dear Friend who has common sense, I'm always going to stand with America. I'm always going to reject the extremes. I'm always going to reject Socialism. I'm always going to fight against the anti-American way of life. And this has enraged a lot of people in the media, in my party, and even former staffers --- disgruntled leakers who are viciously and anonymously attacking me. This is what happens when you put common sense and the wellbeing of the people you are supposed to represent ahead of party loyalty. But most of all, I think this is what happens when you clash with the Socialist movement "DSA!" that is hijacking the Democratic party. They want to... Abolish our borders Abolish the electoral college Abolish Israel Abolish the Senate and the Supreme Court (no, seriously, this is in the "DSA!" platform) That bad news is the "DSA!" crazies have gone from the political fringe to controlling one of America's major political parties—and onto ballots across the country. The good news is the hardworking, common-sense Americans I talk to every day still aren't buying it. I mean, a recent Rasmussen poll kind of proves it: 71% of Americans reject socialism 67% of Democrat voters reject socialism While 82% of Republican voters reject socialism But here's the thing. The loudest voice in the room is often the one that looks the most powerful. And I've got to say, the "DSA!" voices in Washington are loud and getting louder. The media is their megaphone. Which is why you may be under the false impression that people really do want the "DSA!" and their extreme policies Nothing could be further from the truth. **[I'm standing up to them.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMTJ9AAwAAAAAAy-YEiI09GrArJ14OFD6MglLpi3Eax0IW1sL1Gujar-fk1q1i4WyhkNBbwbLxIZtS0F9HUl1OW1T0AuwyutBfKwrXdUKj78wW3Ld6E2EFQ)** But sadly I'm pretty much alone on this side of the aisle. So, can I ask you a favor? Whatever your party affiliation is, can I ask you to stand with me against the daily barrage of hit-pieces **[If you can donate just $25 it would be a big help to me.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMTJ9AAwAAAAAAy-YEiI1aBKdKx0S6ZMDFixB1AdCp7gEzC5gdaPaaQNfTalrMcZAkMPwlKiSm8fw8djjwbzehuX5_lXK-OjRVS-WhCTTYFdyHQEYMvF9dQ)** But it will also send a message. It will show the truth that the "real numbers" are on our side here in Pennsylvania, as well as around the rest of America. You know, I recently stood in front of the iconic U.S. Steel Mill and recorded a video talking about how my friend Dave McCormick and I banded together with President Trump to save this facility and the larger steel industry. But I'm not backing down. Even though I know the media... the "DSA!"... and the party bosses... are going to try even harder to defeat me:
---
**"Fetterman Draws Shadow Primary From Democrats Eager to Replace Him: The Pennsylvania senator has long irked members of his own party" ~ Bloomberg**
---

## Powerful Storm Pummels Northeast
A powerful nor'easter [brought torrential rain, flooding, and strong winds](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFutDAQhJ8GOp_Wa4yhcPE3193fpkSLdzkcGYyMdae8fUSKvEDK0Uij-b6Px_SgmOL-_E-b-LrkaZf3maRWKdOei9BZpayxnisVXoWYwioTAvYKRoVuolDjS6aOWvaLCIppxWs3ggVjtWtX3zkzDtiPVghnNmStzHo0Gpg4IPVt9NcejOg0gNXuptnAvDiLC6IeEZoOhGPN5faZ415XWdJXfkm5hby1ya-1Hmdj_jV4b_BOx4VwVVcoNYYkDd5_YdRZc9lUoENUyKx2eSvZn4l2Vh1YN0vQQdiGbhgMmz4YCM4NvHQa2uL5eMeU4tm7poPnRjH9vKh_lPfy-B0AAP__tqyCwA) to the Northeast on Saturday, and the region is braced for more impact as the weekend continues. Floodwaters [covered streets in coastal New Jersey](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFu7CAURL8Gd7bg2sBSULzG3b42pYXhshBhWAGylb-PvL-Q9ow0ozNfz-1pYor59d8cqLsvW8arJewd65ZLRdM61hB7C6a6gMYZG3ADCmKkagS5GdvjidtiBqc9IuA8oGZSUU5nzuQQtNj5zqUwDBer_Gy9mB-PXSyLYIrtYIao7z6qQDJKOZMTczPdveTgAZgCShaKLvZSp-8Scw_o0085sU62HEPSofd3I_M_AiuB9bquKe_29rjzm6DpASuBtfVSj0ZgvdVus_FDRp9KcTG_xmqz4UopwYaq3fuKKcUmJFno6zAxfQb7H386NfwGAAD__wxYfYY) on Saturday morning, knocking out electricity for more than 70,000 customers and threatening dangerous conditions through the weekend. Forecasters raised [rain projections to 3-6 inches](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u5CAMRp-GdIyM87cpKLZJN9tuGTHBDKwIRODJaN5-xZXuE9zGsmzryOf7e9_uJsSQnn_MQZpd3hK9ayRmKlvKhUxlKj5w9aZYT8aa3dOGgJOEReK8mZ3DRdtgOqsdEVLfkVbzAiP0o5o7r0carBmV2qGn3T0mGBy4YTLTL7Xg0D-6oBsPFpwVwKjmm7I9PNw8okNUC4IYgGzgXG7_ckjsycVPvqjc9nx0UXvms4r-t8BV4Jo-Z67cVgLXBha4wtL6UeD6qrIZtrtvO8m-kGFKVabPLttQ7rnVGC6Sr9MapipzkuxJVs7lkKfPnKss1PRzaryuaHu-Q4yhTrMY4HmYEL8-5B8Ge2n8HwAA__-oeY4K) in New York City. Additional flooding was expected along the Mid-Atlantic coast, particularly near New Jersey and Delaware, according to the National Weather Service. Meanwhile, [Hurricane Nolo](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFu9CAQhJ8Gd7ZgsY9zQfE37u5vU1prWI6NsDkBOStvHzmvkG6kkWb0fR-P9YGc-Hj-x51sC3k96KyJWqOyHrkQ1kYlcqsRi4-EHl2kFSTcejn3YFZ0jd-0jth5G4iAdEdWmVlOUk_KdNHq2QHcx5sy5u63GbewST2NLmgN0zb6ju21J2cwSspJmUF5LbdgJggAagYpRkmeWy7DZ-ajRQrpO7-pDC7vXbKxtVcV-p-ARcBynufgtnpxXL2A5YoCltpy2fsjp9zHr1LY4UF9xBOZBSxdsf51ckpcb0aM8rkjp9-D9kcvbws_AQAA__9TE3fm) strengthened into a Category 2 storm as it approached Hawaii, with the potential to become a "catastrophic" rainmaker.
## Trump Cuts Nearly $1 Billion in Spending
President Trump****[_canceled almost $1 billion in federal funding_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHO3CAUhE-DO6_ww0AoKCL9crdpUyJsHmsiDBa89So5feRcIeVopNF838-ne_qUU3n98AdaitUV_PSMRNhcqQ19J2x7or77Fnb0wW87OuCgRm5G0M5vlC50sx-CjYiAYkA7acMlF3LSw24nw4Ve-RbByNV4H2NArYzCFUCtqx6Svfe4AT1xLif9mILga9QSIsBkgLOZY0hU2-NXTYV2jPl3vbA9tnoM2e5EZ2fiO4OFweLPG-Gu7tAobRkZLNTexzk27FvqPdXSx_guIZUwzmoVUknDlTGoAGTU38SmZ9SIQhrNxOLcFf8w8XVgSO-DgRRfnXwJPteCjurpTv_CPjQbzk_KOXWl2cxfh0_530n6T7eXhb8BAAD__02ojdU) on Friday using the "pocket rescission" process, which allows him to sidestep congressional approval.** ** The largest portion involved $567 million appropriated for the Department of Health and Human Services to provide social services to illegal immigrants, including through grants to non-government organizations. The funds were [_deemed to be no longer necessary_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu2zAMRb9G3hhIdPz8PGjo4i1dOxqMRNlsZcmQ5AT5-8L9hW4EL-4Bzv31WB4kUdL6k3a2LeQl8btGbo3LknJhqo3LJq1uVPzG5MltvKDGL9AT4LiQa_Li5U6dt4EZue_YmnHSg-4HM3abxclP_tvde-r5yRN96wGNMyNj6Jm968RePD3haLQezHgzvtfPMA4YEM2EWt01e2m53H5nSW3jED_5xeXm8t5Fu7V2VNX_UDgrnNPnyLVdkcL5Aiuc9XTdg8L5rHAZKpxbOfcDHCXH8XpSiR8wT5AE4Uxe0gohF5AYeaUIsu-yFkqtAiUPhRxDyO6s7OEoeS2016ub-A1Hdn-4QeHqpFbJSeHcFeuPt8Qo9WtUd73uJPGfQPvP3V8W_wYAAP__NWGZ0w) because of the near-elimination of illegal border crossings in the past year.** ** Other cuts [_aligned with Trump 's anti-DEI agenda_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1u6zAQBODTUJ0McvXDp4LFa9Q5bUphLS7NDSjSINc2cvtAuULqD5jBzOd1uyInzvcPPMhJKFumd0skQnXLpRI2oRpZWsTqI6HHPdIGGuZeLz3YDXfhF20jdt4FIqChI2fsoic9TMZ20Q2IMxGYYMP8TwMsxoz7GGi0OgTc547dmacXsEbrydiL8YO-BTtBADALaDVq8iylXr4KZ4kU0nd5Ub3s5eiSiyKPpob_ClYFq0SKnNJpCtZYDjonKVjRH5y5SUXhkhWsszFg7dJLfR6Pfse8U2r9jVPikvtAniqmPjyz53xXsHbV-cf75DZbNer7gfzb08kfr3s5-AkAAP__pZGEMw), including sex-change procedure research, minority business development, and the Department of Justice's Community Relations Services, which the White House said promoted identity-conscious law enforcement practices.

**Whatever happened to Shakey's Pizza?** Before Pizza Hut and Domino's conquered the American pizza market, Shakey's Pizza Parlor was the original, the nation's first franchised pizza chain, and for a generation of teenagers, it was the only place to be on a Friday night. Sherwood "Shakey" Johnson and his buddy Ed Plummer opened the first Shakey's in Sacramento in 1954 in a converted grocery store. Johnson, a Navy veteran whose wartime bout with malaria left him with a tremor and his nickname, had a simple formula: pizza, cold beer, and live Dixieland jazz. It worked. By the mid-1970s, Shakey's had grown to close to 500 U.S. locations, coast to coast. [You can see an early ad here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO6yAQheGnwV0sPICJC4pIV2nuZquVtrTGZghExER4Yitvv8q-wrbnSF_xf1_GC6aclusn3slxKONC-5qJmeq4lEq4MtWYeI1YfST0OEcaQUJ_kMMB7Igzp41GjY13gQhINeQ6O0gjlelsEx30RhskmEDpKQCFwQxkCI9H7K3W1CT39uQAtpPSdLbtvJJTsAYCQDeAFFqST1xqeytp4Ughv8pGtZ3LvckuMj9WoU4CzgLO-763r_Lk50Tv_70gz1Go8ybUP_VVH7f_lE8fc1Odf-wp57T2Vmh5vWPKvyT_scTm4CcAAP__wyZyQw). But the real magic was the atmosphere. Banjo players and ragtime pianists performed on small stages. Silent comedy shorts, the Three Stooges, Laurel and Hardy, flickered on screens between sets and hushed the kids instantly. Menus printed [song lyrics so families could sing along](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFqwzAQxvGnkbcY6WRH8aChUNIuKXQKZDFn6RSpKFaQLzZ5-5K-Qtfvg9_wP5_GE6ac5usX3shyKONM25KJmeo4l0q4MNWYeIlYfST06CKNIGG_k8MOzIiO00pjh423gQhIN2SVGWQvda9MEy0eDtOBJj1J0CaQNgqpA60mR-CDM02yL08OYJSUvTKt8lpOwfQQANQAUnSSfOJS25-SZo4U8rOsVFtXbk22kfm-CP0m4CjguG1b-ywPfkz0-l8LsotCH1eh3y87_zlf4vnj2zXV-vuWck7L3ohOXm-Y8h_J_yyxWvgNAAD__x9EcpI). Pinball rooms gave way to arcades in the 1980s. The motto said it all: _"We serve fun at Shakey's... also pizza."_ For teenagers, Shakey's was the Friday night ritual. After the high school football game, kids piled in to grab a booth, split a pizza, flirt, feed quarters into the arcade machines, and soak up the noise. A separate "beerless" room kept teens and adults comfortably apart. Birthday parties were practically a rite of passage. Then came the ownership carousel. After Johnson and Plummer sold out in the late 1960s, Shakey's passed through a string of neglectful corporate owners. Each squeezed the brand and invested nothing. Meanwhile, Pizza Hut, Domino's, and Little Caesars offered speed, delivery, and lower prices. The banjo players quietly disappeared. By 2003, just 61 U.S. locations remained. Today, about 43 Shakey's survive in the U.S., nearly all in Southern California. The real twist? Shakey's is thriving overseas, [with roughly 295 locations in the Philippines](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykzzFuwyAUgOHTwBbr8YxNGBi6ZEvXjoiYR6DFxgJqK7ev2iv0AP8vfR93e3cpp-357lYyPRS70dky9U7VbqWSa51qTL1FV30k590SySLgfAF9QWXd0tNBVjruTSBCGjkZoTRMME5C8WiuoDVN6qFm0ir40aGUi5aPWYtAQV15Mr8_0KgEwCTUIPwIj6AmDIhCIzAJ5FMvdfgsaeuRQn6Vg-qwlJVnE3vfGxvfGN4Y3s7zHFp0X_Rqz1q-92GPDG-8Gr-fKefUZsUkPFeX8l_f_8k-DP4EAAD__783bDc), where it is a publicly traded company. A new 1980s-themed flagship opened in Culver City, California, last year, complete with arcade games and retro décor, betting that Americans still miss the parlor that started it all. _Did you ever pile into a Shakey's after a Friday night football game? What do you remember most, the pizza, the camaraderie, or the banjo player? Hit reply and tell us._

Before Pizza Hut and Domino's conquered the American pizza market, Shakey's Pizza Parlor was the original, the nation's first franchised pizza chain, and for a generation of teenagers, it was the only place to be on a Friday night. Sherwood "Shakey" Johnson and his buddy Ed Plummer opened the first Shakey's in Sacramento in 1954 in a converted grocery store. Johnson, a Navy veteran whose wartime bout with malaria left him with a tremor and his nickname, had a simple formula: pizza, cold beer, and live Dixieland jazz. It worked. By the mid-1970s, Shakey's had grown to close to 500 U.S. locations, coast to coast. . But the real magic was the atmosphere. Banjo players and ragtime pianists performed on small stages. Silent comedy shorts, the Three Stooges, Laurel and Hardy, flickered on screens between sets and hushed the kids instantly. Menus printed . Pinball rooms gave way to arcades in the 1980s. The motto said it all: "We serve fun at Shakey's... also pizza." For teenagers, Shakey's was the Friday night ritual. After the high school football game, kids piled in to grab a booth, split a pizza, flirt, feed quarters into the arcade machines, and soak up the noise. A separate "beerless" room kept teens and adults comfortably apart. Birthday parties were practically a rite of passage. Then came the ownership carousel. After Johnson and Plummer sold out in the late 1960s, Shakey's passed through a string of neglectful corporate owners. Each squeezed the brand and invested nothing. Meanwhile, Pizza Hut, Domino's, and Little Caesars offered speed, delivery, and lower prices. The banjo players quietly disappeared. By 2003, just 61 U.S. locations remained. Today, about 43 Shakey's survive in the U.S., nearly all in Southern California. The real twist? Shakey's is thriving overseas, , where it is a publicly traded company. A new 1980s-themed flagship opened in Culver City, California, last year, complete with arcade games and retro décor, betting that Americans still miss the parlor that started it all. clean_body: Peter, My name is Emily, and I'm a ballot chaser for Turning Point PAC in Arizona. That means every day, I show up, knock on doors, have conversations with potential voters, and chase down ballots before Election Day. I need to tell you what I'm seeing out here, because I don't think most people understand how close this really is. Arizona is not lost.Not even close. But it is not safe either. A new poll just showed Katie Hobbs up by 4 points over Andy Biggs. Four points. That is the entire ballgame, sitting right there behind the doors I have not knocked on yet. Turning Point PAC is not like anything else in this space. They take decades of grassroots organizing and put real people, like me, into these communities well before Election Day. We build relationships. We knock on the same doors more than once. We chase every ballot, mail-in or in person, because every single one counts. This is the vision Charlie Kirk built. People on the ground, having real conversations, changing real minds. And it is working! But I cannot do this alone, and neither can the 700 of us out here across Arizona. I 'm seeing momentum on the ground, but we have so many more voters to cover. We can't do it without your continued support. Every $50 you give sponsors a ballot chaser like me for one full day. Sisters and Brothers –
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=108%2E42639%2E-C7-Dt)
[](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/28?c0=deluzio-em-jun26.AE9VfX&refcode=em260927&refcode2=108.42639.-C7-Dt&t=2&akid=108%2E42639%2E-C7-Dt)
---
Sisters and Brothers –
The political future of our country rests upon one very simple principle: the need for working people to stand together and fight back against corporate greed, and create an economy that works for all of us, and not just billionaires and large corporations.
So when we have progressive candidates with the guts to take on corporate power in this country, we have to do what we can to support them if we are going to have any chance at transforming this country and creating a government that works for all of us.
**One of those people is Congressman Chris Deluzio in Pennsylvania.**
Chris understands that our current healthcare system is broken and wildly expensive. He believes, as I do, that healthcare is a human right, not a privilege, and that we must end the embarrassment of being the only major country on earth that does not guarantee healthcare to every man, woman and child. That is why he supports Medicare for All.
Chris understands that we have a corrupt campaign finance system which allows the very rich and their super PACs to buy and sell politicians. That is why he fights vigorously to end the disastrous Citizens United Supreme Court decision — which allows Big Money to control our political process.
Chris understands that too many workers in America are earning starvation wages. That is why he fights to raise the minimum wage to a living wage, to make it easier for workers to join unions, to build the millions of units of low income and affordable housing this country desperately needs and make sure that seniors can retire with dignity and security.
Sisters and brothers, Chris' campaign is about more than just one single House seat. His work is about taking on the powerful special interests that dominate our economic and political life.
And keeping him in Congress requires all of us to do our part to make it happen. And that is why I am once again asking for your financial support.

name: John Fetterman
subject: I'm always going to reject Socialism and the anti-American way of life
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY FETTERMAN FOR PA
body:
They are calling me "Benedict Arnold, but lazy"

lies, half-truths, innuendos, and
smears...

View in Web Browser
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e602966/UaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvUGZoSmUydEVVbg/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA5Mjc/LbmNsejFCdGw5ZA/qP2hpZHM9bmNSdlBTRzFiSE1EbHhsc10/garkZcw/sbh44d58afe

[Image showing logo and first aid]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Dear Patriot who has common sense,

I'm always going to stand with America.

I'm always going to reject the extremes.

I'm always going to reject Socialism.

I'm always going to fight against the anti-American way of life.

And this has enraged a lot of people in the media, in my party, and
even former staffers --- disgruntled leakers who are viciously and
anonymously attacking me.

This is what happens when you put common sense and the wellbeing of
the people you are supposed to represent ahead of party loyalty.

But most of all, I think this is what happens when you clash with the
Socialist movement "DSA!" that is hijacking the Democratic party.

They want to...

Abolish our borders

Abolish the electoral college

Abolish Israel

Abolish the Senate and the Supreme Court (no, seriously, this is in
the "DSA!" platform)

That bad news is the "DSA!" crazies have gone from the political
fringe to controlling one of America's major political parties—and
onto ballots across the country.

The good news is the hardworking, common-sense Americans I talk to
every day still aren't buying it.

I mean, a recent Rasmussen poll kind of proves it:

71% of Americans reject socialism

67% of Democrat voters reject socialism

While 82% of Republican voters reject socialism

But here's the thing. The loudest voice in the room is often the one
that looks the most powerful.

And I've got to say, the "DSA!" voices in Washington are loud and
getting louder. The media is their megaphone.

Which is why you may be under the false impression that people really
do want the "DSA!" and their extreme policies

Nothing could be further from the truth.

I'M STANDING UP TO THEM.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

But sadly I'm pretty much alone on this side of the aisle.

So, can I ask you a favor?

Whatever your party affiliation is, can I ask you to stand with me
against the daily barrage of hit-pieces

IF YOU CAN DONATE JUST $25 IT WOULD BE A BIG HELP TO ME.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

But it will also send a message. It will show the truth that the
"real numbers" are on our side here in Pennsylvania, as well as around
the rest of America.

You know, I recently stood in front of the iconic U.S. Steel Mill and
recorded a video talking about how my friend Dave McCormick and I
banded together with President Trump to save this facility and the
larger steel industry. But I'm not backing down.

Even though I know the media... the "DSA!"... and the party
bosses... are going to try even harder to defeat me:

"FETTERMAN DRAWS SHADOW PRIMARY FROM DEMOCRATS EAGER TO REPLACE HIM:
THE PENNSYLVANIA SENATOR HAS LONG IRKED MEMBERS OF HIS OWN PARTY" ~
BLOOMBERG

If you'll stand with me today, I know we can show them that we're not
backing down and that the real numbers are on the side of common sense
and putting our country first.

Thank you!

John Fetterman

P.S. - I'll bet you're more than a little surprised to get this email
from me. So, I want to say thanks for setting aside party affiliation
for a second and hearing me out. You see, I'm not a progressive. And
I'm definitely not a Democratic Socialist. I'm just a senator with a
big mouth who happens to stand for common-sense things like... strong
borders, safe streets, a powerful economy, bringing jobs to my
constituents, and Israel and Ukraine's right to defend themselves, not
to mention the basic machinery of our democracy (the Electoral
College, the Senate, and the Supreme Court). If you see eye-to-eye
with me, then I could sure use your help. The "DSA!" vision for
Pennsylvania and for America is not a healthy one. It is a dangerous
one.Common-sense people need to join together now to reject this
vision before it's too late. CAN I COUNT ON YOU TO STAND WITH ME
TODAY?

Abolish our borders Abolish the electoral college Abolish Israel Abolish the Senate and the Supreme Court (no, seriously, this is in the "DSA!" platform) That bad news is the "DSA!" crazies have gone from the political fringe to controlling one of America's major political parties—and onto ballots across the country. The good news is the hardworking, common-sense Americans I talk to every day still aren't buying it. I mean, a recent Rasmussen poll kind of proves it: 71% of Americans reject socialism 67% of Democrat voters reject socialism While 82% of Republican voters reject socialism But here's the thing. The loudest voice in the room is often the one that looks the most powerful. And I've got to say, the "DSA!" voices in Washington are loud and getting louder. The media is their megaphone. Which is why you may be under the false impression that people really do want the "DSA!" and their extreme policies Nothing could be further from the truth. I'M STANDING UP TO THEM. [ But sadly I'm pretty much alone on this side of the aisle. So, can I ask you a favor? Whatever your party affiliation is, can I ask you to stand with me against the daily barrage of hit-pieces IF YOU CAN DONATE JUST $25 IT WOULD BE A BIG HELP TO ME. [ But it will also send a message. It will show the truth that the "real numbers" are on our side here in Pennsylvania, as well as around the rest of America. You know, I recently stood in front of the iconic U.S. Steel Mill and recorded a video talking about how my friend Dave McCormick and I banded together with President Trump to save this facility and the larger steel industry. But I'm not backing down. Even though I know the media... the "DSA!"... and the party bosses... are going to try even harder to defeat me: "FETTERMAN DRAWS SHADOW PRIMARY FROM DEMOCRATS EAGER TO REPLACE HIM: THE PENNSYLVANIA SENATOR HAS LONG IRKED MEMBERS OF HIS OWN PARTY" ~ BLOOMBERG If you'll stand with me today, I know we can show them that we're not backing down and that the real numbers are on the side of common sense and putting our country first. Thank you! John Fetterman P.S. - I'll bet you're more than a little surprised to get this email from me. So, I want to say thanks for setting aside party affiliation for a second and hearing me out. You see, I'm not a progressive. And I'm definitely not a Democratic Socialist. I'm just a senator with a big mouth who happens to stand for common-sense things like... strong borders, safe streets, a powerful economy, bringing jobs to my constituents, and Israel and Ukraine's right to defend themselves, not to mention the basic machinery of our democracy (the Electoral College, the Senate, and the Supreme Court). If you see eye-to-eye with me, then I could sure use your help. The "DSA!" vision for Pennsylvania and for America is not a healthy one. It is a dangerous one.Common-sense people need to join together now to reject this vision before it's too late. CAN I COUNT ON YOU TO STAND WITH ME TODAY? Adam Hamilton, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, greets Jerilynn Henrikson on August 20, 2026 at Gravel City Roasters in Emporia, Ks. Henrikson said she is a lifelong Democrat and said, "I know I don't want Marshall." Photo: Clayton Steward
_Story by Clayton Steward and Justin Perkins_
Adam Hamilton, pastor and founder of Church of the Resurrection in the Kansas City suburbs, the largest United Methodist congregation in the United States, walked into a coffee shop in Emporia, Kansas, in late August. With a population of 24,000, Emporia is roughly the same size as Resurrection's membership. But instead of preaching, Hamilton was there to make his case for why he can flip a seat for the U.S. Senate from the Sunflower State, a feat more than 90 years in the making.
Hamilton told the crowd of about 40 people his campaign is rooted in his faith and experiences as a pastor but clarified that he is not running to force people to be Christian or United Methodist. Instead, he is motivated to uphold the U.S. Constitution and fight for individual rights.
He shared a conversation he had with his wife many times last year.
"Somebody's got to do something," he told her while Trump's cabinet implemented One Big Beautiful Bill policies and cut funding to groups such as the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID). "After about eight months of saying somebody's got to do something, she finally turned to me in January this year and she said, 'Maybe you need to do something.'"
_Drop Site 's ongoing collaboration with Barn Raiser [puts a focus on rural politics](https://substack.com/redirect/40bcb207-db1a-497d-adaa-191ca61c2087?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with a newsletter running through November._
[Sign Up Here](https://substack.com/redirect/40bcb207-db1a-497d-adaa-191ca61c2087?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## **Religion and politics collide**
A man in a Navy hat raised his hand at the meet and greet in Emporia. He explained the day before he had met with his friends of 30 years at the coffee shop Hamilton's stop was being held at.
"They're Republican, I'm a Democrat. We get along. We have coffee. We go places together and talk and talk," he said. The man had told his friends about coming to Hamilton's campaign stop.
"They said, 'He's woke.' I said, 'Well, wasn't Jesus woke?' "
Hamilton's 36-year career as the pastor of a mainline Protestant congregation puts him in an unusual position as a first-time Democratic candidate. In a race with sharp political divisions and an enduring rural-urban divide, he is attempting to bridge a wide coalition of voters based on the ethics of his theological commitments.
And since he won the ten-person Democratic primary in August, Republicans have sought to wield Christianity against him. They say he is "too woke" for Kansas and have even [called him a heretic](https://substack.com/redirect/e7fc6a1f-bfd7-4e24-8cdf-8d46b559e907?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for suggesting God would not condemn people who are not Christians.
This messaging came to a head September 14, when Vice President J.D. Vance appeared at a campaign rally in Olathe, Kansas, to support Hamilton's Republican opponent, Sen. Roger Marshall.
Vance accused Hamilton's church of supporting a group of devil worshipers because of their sponsorship of the Kansas City PrideFest this year. The pride event included the satirical drag queen performance group Our Ladies of Perpetual Indulgence, which Vance labeled an "anti-Christian hate group."
The vice president also cherry-picked two 2020 sermons, one in which Hamilton talked about the Black Lives Matter movement and white privilege, and another where said Christians need to repent for their destruction of the environment and acknowledged "maybe changing your diet" as one action.
"Democrat pastor Adam Hamilton thinks it's a sin to be white and a sin to raise cattle and eat meat, but he's okay with supporting groups that spit on god-fearing Americans and mock everything that we hold dear," Vance told the audience. "Ladies and gentlemen, that is not Christianity. That is left-wing radicalism dressed in the skin suit of our religion."
In a video response released on September 16, Hamilton said Vance's comments were part of the "broken politics" that define Washington. As he has done on the campaign trail, Hamilton presented his D.C. outsider status as the fix.
"These attacks on our faith," he said, "are false and are a sad attempt to distract from the real hardship facing Kansans." He did not address Resurrection's support of the KC PrideFest, although the church's website features a [dedicated page](https://substack.com/redirect/7ce747f4-845d-44e2-bccb-8a7a8a06c275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for its LGBTQ ministry, which says, "Resurrection is an LGBTQ friendly church."
Hamilton's response to the vice president instead highlighted Resurrection's food and health care assistance programs, which the church claims has aided more than 45,000 people.
"Trying to demean or marginalize the faith of other people, that's just wrong," he said. "It's also against the Christian teachings to love, serve and care for one another."
In a 2021 podcast called [Changing My Position](https://substack.com/redirect/af398929-9378-4fa2-b868-e044067a19ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Hamilton put his position on sexuality more clearly. He said that he had spent conservatively "20,000 hours studying the Bible." As a result, he found, "What is crystal clear is that the driving ethic of the Christian faith is love, and we're going to love and welcome people here, gay or straight."
His campaign now depends on whether or not voters resonate with that ethic extending to the political arena. "I lead from the center," he told the group gathered in Emporia. "I pastor a church with 9,000 Republicans, 9,000 Democrats and 7,000 independents. I love those Republicans."
## **" Doc" Marshall**
In a debate before hundreds at the Kansas state fair September 12, Hamilton's incumbent Republican opponent Roger Marshall launched a similar line of attack.
Born in El Dorado, Kansas, Marshall practiced medicine as an obstetrician-gynecologist in Great Bend, Kansas, in Barton County, for more than 25 years. Marshall was first elected to Congress in 2016 to serve Kansas' rural 1st Congressional District until he was elected to the Senate in 2021. Endorsed by Trump, Marshall contrasts his rural bona fides against Hamilton's suburban background.
"My opponent is too woke, he's too weak and he doesn't stand for anything," Marshall said. He blamed the Democratic party for having "strangled the ag industry," saying that if Hamilton had his way, "he'd go put a plastic bag over the mouths of these dairy cows back here," motioning to the livestock building on the fairgrounds.
Despite his spar with Hamilton, Marshall spent much of the debate struggling against the crowd. Videos recorded of the debate showed Marshall's answers overwhelmed by jeers and boos from the crowd.
Days earlier, the New York Times reported that Marshall and his OBGYN practice had sued more than 700 patients over their inability to pay for care. Eighty-one of those cases resulted in arrests, including a couple who were arrested on Easter weekend for being unable to pay a $4,561 bill for an emergency hysterectomy.
The Times found Marshall routinely charged patients an 18% annual interest rate on unpaid bills ranging from $101 to several thousand dollars. Patients also had their paychecks and bank accounts garnished. Most of the patients sued lived in rural Barton County, including many who lacked insurance.
At the state fair, Marshall attempted to defend his billing record, saying "those were common, common business practices. We would go a year before we would ever send somebody over." But the crowd was not buying it and erupted in chants of "shame on you!"
## **A vital seat for Democrats**
Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 1932, when George McGill was elected during the Great Depression. But voters have elected some high-profile Democrats in recent years, including two-term Gov. Laura Kelly and four-term U.S. Rep. Sharice Davids.
Hamilton believes he can join them by pushing a platform of broad appeal: lowering costs, strengthening consumer protection laws, stopping D.C. corruption and combating the tariffs and health care cuts championed by President Donald Trump in the One Big Beautiful Bill.
If Democrats hold all their current senate seats and can flip four held by Republicans, they can retake the Senate in November.
While Marshall remains the favorite, recent polls show an unexpectedly tight race for Republicans. A [September poll by Emerson College Polling/Nexstar Media](https://substack.com/redirect/3ef277fc-7d03-406a-b9c4-a4ef7ddb974b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) gives Hamilton a two-point lead over Marshall. It is the first independent survey of the cycle to show Hamilton leading.
"This poll finds Democrats with their best chance to win their first Senate seat in Kansas since 1932, in part driven by Democrat Hamilton's appeal to independent voters, leading by 15 points," said Spencer Kimball, executive director of Emerson College Polling, in a statement accompanying the survey. The poll of likely voters also found 8% are undecided, with 4% supporting Libertarian David Graham. About half of respondents identified the economy as their top issue.
In August, Cook Political Report shifted the Kansas race in Hamilton's favor from "solid Republican" to "lean Republican."
A July poll by GBAO Strategies in Washington D.C. found Marshall's close affiliation with President Trump hurt his favorability. Over half of the polled individuals said they do not want a "yes man" for Trump elected as their next senator.
In a sign of shifting party divisions, former Kansas GOP Governor Bill Graves [endorsed Hamilton](https://substack.com/redirect/5016cfe0-6b7c-4f0f-b75e-5ffa81fde952?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in late September, saying Marshall simply amounted to a "yes-vote" for the Trump administration. At the same time, Hamilton urged former Vice President Kamala Harris to stay out of his campaign, saying in an interview with MS NOW, "We are a different kind of Democrat."
Flipping a key seat requires not only campaign stops, endorsements and good polling numbers, but also money. Hamilton told the Emporia coffee shop crowd it will take $20 million to run a successful campaign. The crowd let out cheers when he asked if they had heard of a guy named Talarico.
"You're a cheap date in Kansas," a New York donor told Hamilton when comparing his $20 million goal to Talarico's $160 million goal.
Hamilton has raised just over $4 million, largely from individuals, according to FEC filings. Marshall has raised more than $6 million including $2.7 million in support from PACs ranging from the Mississippi Farm Bureau and the health care industry to the Teamsters Union PAC.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5053c657-dc67-4d05-8f5b-c27bf05e7339?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Adam Hamilton, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, is interviewed before speaking on August 20, 2026 at Gravel City Roasters in Emporia, Ks. Photo: Clayton Steward.
## **Who will represent rural Kansas?**
"I was raised in Johnson County," Hamilton told the crowd in Emporia. "I'm really sorry about that," poking fun at his childhood in suburban Kansas City. It's a much different Kansas experience than much of Kansas where rolling hills are dotted with pump jacks, cattle, late summer wildflowers, and wind turbines this time of year.
Hamilton feels like he is gaining the pulse of rural Kansas after an estimated 40 campaign stops across the state before Emporia.
"Our ag industry is the number one industry in the state," he said in an interview with Barn Raiser. "If you as a senator are not caring about ag and the ag industry and the people in rural America, you're not doing your job."
For his part, Marshall spent most of August traveling across 59 Kansas counties speaking with farmers, ranchers, doctors, manufacturers, small business owners and families as part of his "120 Stops to Strengthen Rural Kansas" tour.
He is concerned about the high costs for fuel and fertilizer as well as the impacts tariffs have on farmers and ranchers. The decision to lift tariffs and import foreign beef had not been announced at the time of that interview.
Hamilton is also concerned about the state of rural hospitals. Kansas leads the nation in rural hospitals that are at risk of immediate closure due to the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill last year. Marshall championed his vote for the bill at the time, which made nearly $1 trillion in cuts to Medicaid through 2035. In 2025, United Methodist Health Ministry Fund estimated that Kansas stood to lose nearly $4 billion in federal and state Medicaid funding.
The bill also provided a one-time $50 billion distributed over five years in the Rural Health Transformation Program. Kansas received $221 million for the program's first year, far short of the funds needed to offset the Medicaid cuts.
In 2024, over 240,000 Kansans were uninsured, a statistically higher rate than the rest of the country.
In a statement released after his rural Kansas tour, Marshall said, "We've got a lot to be proud of--from cutting taxes for working families and growing Kansas manufacturing to delivering real resources for our rural hospitals.
Will a politics of human decency outweigh party loyalty among voters?
Hamilton believes so. At a campaign stop in Greensburg, he recalled one woman who told him, "I want somebody who's going to help me not hate my neighbors anymore," he told the crowd in Emporia.
Short-haired, elderly women held down the front row of chairs while Hamilton spoke. They occasionally responded to a question posed by Hamilton, regularly giving a classic Midwestern shake of the head in support or disgust.
Among those in the front row was former English teacher, Sharol Cutrell. After Hamilton spoke, she told him she didn't vote for him in the primaries.
"I would vote for him today," she told Barn Raiser. "Everything I believe, he's right in line with. And we need somebody like that, somebody neutral, who's for people who don't have as much as we do."
Cutrell had concerns about voting for a megachurch pastor in the primary, a sentiment shared by others in the coffee shop that morning. Seeing him in person made her believe he is the right nominee for the challenge.
When introducing themselves to Hamilton, many folks gave a brief outline of their family tree, starting with their abolitionist and settler roots in Kansas. A sunflower was incorporated into the design of the banner on the Lyon County Democrats office across the street.
In November voters will choose between two fifth-generation Kansans: a MAGA-backed Republican doctor and a Democrat mainline Protestant pastor.
"Keep me in your prayers," Hamilton said to a woman as he left the event.

clean_body: Kansas pastor Adam Hamilton is challenging party lines in a tight Senate race. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Kansas pastor Adam Hamilton is challenging party lines in a tight Senate race. | | | Sep 27| | | ∙| | Guest post ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Adam Hamilton, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, greets Jerilynn Henrikson on August 20, 2026 at Gravel City Roasters in Emporia, Ks. Henrikson said she is a lifelong Democrat and said, "I know I don't want Marshall." Photo: Clayton Steward Story by Clayton Steward and Justin Perkins Adam Hamilton, pastor and founder of Church of the Resurrection in the Kansas City suburbs, the largest United Methodist congregation in the United States, walked into a coffee shop in Emporia, Kansas, in late August. With a population of 24,000, Emporia is roughly the same size as Resurrection's membership. But instead of preaching, Hamilton was there to make his case for why he can flip a seat for the U.S. Senate from the Sunflower State, a feat more than 90 years in the making. Hamilton told the crowd of about 40 people his campaign is rooted in his faith and experiences as a pastor but clarified that he is not running to force people to be Christian or United Methodist. Instead, he is motivated to uphold the U.S. Constitution and fight for individual rights. He shared a conversation he had with his wife many times last year. "Somebody's got to do something," he told her while Trump's cabinet implemented One Big Beautiful Bill policies and cut funding to groups such as the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID). "After about eight months of saying somebody's got to do something, she finally turned to me in January this year and she said, 'Maybe you need to do something.'" Drop Site 's ongoing collaboration with Barn Raiser with a newsletter running through November. Religion and politics collide A man in a Navy hat raised his hand at the meet and greet in Emporia. He explained the day before he had met with his friends of 30 years at the coffee shop Hamilton's stop was being held at. "They're Republican, I'm a Democrat. We get along. We have coffee. We go places together and talk and talk," he said. The man had told his friends about coming to Hamilton's campaign stop. "They said, 'He's woke.' I said, 'Well, wasn't Jesus woke?' " Hamilton's 36-year career as the pastor of a mainline Protestant congregation puts him in an unusual position as a first-time Democratic candidate. In a race with sharp political divisions and an enduring rural-urban divide, he is attempting to bridge a wide coalition of voters based on the ethics of his theological commitments. And since he won the ten-person Democratic primary in August, Republicans have sought to wield Christianity against him. They say he is "too woke" for Kansas and have even for suggesting God would not condemn people who are not Christians. This messaging came to a head September 14, when Vice President J.D. Vance appeared at a campaign rally in Olathe, Kansas, to support Hamilton's Republican opponent, Sen. Roger Marshall. Vance accused Hamilton's church of supporting a group of devil worshipers because of their sponsorship of the Kansas City PrideFest this year. The pride event included the satirical drag queen performance group Our Ladies of Perpetual Indulgence, which Vance labeled an "anti-Christian hate group." The vice president also cherry-picked two 2020 sermons, one in which Hamilton talked about the Black Lives Matter movement and white privilege, and another where said Christians need to repent for their destruction of the environment and acknowledged "maybe changing your diet" as one action. "Democrat pastor Adam Hamilton thinks it's a sin to be white and a sin to raise cattle and eat meat, but he's okay with supporting groups that spit on god-fearing Americans and mock everything that we hold dear," Vance told the audience. "Ladies and gentlemen, that is not Christianity. That is left-wing radicalism dressed in the skin suit of our religion." In a video response released on September 16, Hamilton said Vance's comments were part of the "broken politics" that define Washington. As he has done on the campaign trail, Hamilton presented his D.C. outsider status as the fix. "These attacks on our faith," he said, "are false and are a sad attempt to distract from the real hardship facing Kansans." He did not address Resurrection's support of the KC PrideFest, although the church's website features a for its LGBTQ ministry, which says, "Resurrection is an LGBTQ friendly church." Hamilton's response to the vice president instead highlighted Resurrection's food and health care assistance programs, which the church claims has aided more than 45,000 people. "Trying to demean or marginalize the faith of other people, that's just wrong," he said. "It's also against the Christian teachings to love, serve and care for one another." In a 2021 podcast called , Hamilton put his position on sexuality more clearly. He said that he had spent conservatively "20,000 hours studying the Bible." As a result, he found, "What is crystal clear is that the driving ethic of the Christian faith is love, and we're going to love and welcome people here, gay or straight." His campaign now depends on whether or not voters resonate with that ethic extending to the political arena. "I lead from the center," he told the group gathered in Emporia. "I pastor a church with 9,000 Republicans, 9,000 Democrats and 7,000 independents. I love those Republicans." " Doc" Marshall In a debate before hundreds at the Kansas state fair September 12, Hamilton's incumbent Republican opponent Roger Marshall launched a similar line of attack. Born in El Dorado, Kansas, Marshall practiced medicine as an obstetrician-gynecologist in Great Bend, Kansas, in Barton County, for more than 25 years. Marshall was first elected to Congress in 2016 to serve Kansas' rural 1st Congressional District until he was elected to the Senate in 2021. Endorsed by Trump, Marshall contrasts his rural bona fides against Hamilton's suburban background. "My opponent is too woke, he's too weak and he doesn't stand for anything," Marshall said. He blamed the Democratic party for having "strangled the ag industry," saying that if Hamilton had his way, "he'd go put a plastic bag over the mouths of these dairy cows back here," motioning to the livestock building on the fairgrounds. Despite his spar with Hamilton, Marshall spent much of the debate struggling against the crowd. Videos recorded of the debate showed Marshall's answers overwhelmed by jeers and boos from the crowd. Days earlier, the New York Times reported that Marshall and his OBGYN practice had sued more than 700 patients over their inability to pay for care. Eighty-one of those cases resulted in arrests, including a couple who were arrested on Easter weekend for being unable to pay a $4,561 bill for an emergency hysterectomy. The Times found Marshall routinely charged patients an 18% annual interest rate on unpaid bills ranging from $101 to several thousand dollars. Patients also had their paychecks and bank accounts garnished. Most of the patients sued lived in rural Barton County, including many who lacked insurance. At the state fair, Marshall attempted to defend his billing record, saying "those were common, common business practices. We would go a year before we would ever send somebody over." But the crowd was not buying it and erupted in chants of "shame on you!" A vital seat for Democrats Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 1932, when George McGill was elected during the Great Depression. But voters have elected some high-profile Democrats in recent years, including two-term Gov. Laura Kelly and four-term U.S. Rep. Sharice Davids. Hamilton believes he can join them by pushing a platform of broad appeal: lowering costs, strengthening consumer protection laws, stopping D.C. corruption and combating the tariffs and health care cuts championed by President Donald Trump in the One Big Beautiful Bill. If Democrats hold all their current senate seats and can flip four held by Republicans, they can retake the Senate in November. While Marshall remains the favorite, recent polls show an unexpectedly tight race for Republicans. A gives Hamilton a two-point lead over Marshall. It is the first independent survey of the cycle to show Hamilton leading. "This poll finds Democrats with their best chance to win their first Senate seat in Kansas since 1932, in part driven by Democrat Hamilton's appeal to independent voters, leading by 15 points," said Spencer Kimball, executive director of Emerson College Polling, in a statement accompanying the survey. The poll of likely voters also found 8% are undecided, with 4% supporting Libertarian David Graham. About half of respondents identified the economy as their top issue. In August, Cook Political Report shifted the Kansas race in Hamilton's favor from "solid Republican" to "lean Republican." A July poll by GBAO Strategies in Washington D.C. found Marshall's close affiliation with President Trump hurt his favorability. Over half of the polled individuals said they do not want a "yes man" for Trump elected as their next senator. In a sign of shifting party divisions, former Kansas GOP Governor Bill Graves in late September, saying Marshall simply amounted to a "yes-vote" for the Trump administration. At the same time, Hamilton urged former Vice President Kamala Harris to stay out of his campaign, saying in an interview with MS NOW, "We are a different kind of Democrat." Flipping a key seat requires not only campaign stops, endorsements and good polling numbers, but also money. Hamilton told the Emporia coffee shop crowd it will take $20 million to run a successful campaign. The crowd let out cheers when he asked if they had heard of a guy named Talarico. "You're a cheap date in Kansas," a New York donor told Hamilton when comparing his $20 million goal to Talarico's $160 million goal. Hamilton has raised just over $4 million, largely from individuals, according to FEC filings. Marshall has raised more than $6 million including $2.7 million in support from PACs ranging from the Mississippi Farm Bureau and the health care industry to the Teamsters Union PAC. | | ---|---|--- Adam Hamilton, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, is interviewed before speaking on August 20, 2026 at Gravel City Roasters in Emporia, Ks. Photo: Clayton Steward. Who will represent rural Kansas? "I was raised in Johnson County," Hamilton told the crowd in Emporia. "I'm really sorry about that," poking fun at his childhood in suburban Kansas City. It's a much different Kansas experience than much of Kansas where rolling hills are dotted with pump jacks, cattle, late summer wildflowers, and wind turbines this time of year. Hamilton feels like he is gaining the pulse of rural Kansas after an estimated 40 campaign stops across the state before Emporia. "Our ag industry is the number one industry in the state," he said in an interview with Barn Raiser. "If you as a senator are not caring about ag and the ag industry and the people in rural America, you're not doing your job." For his part, Marshall spent most of August traveling across 59 Kansas counties speaking with farmers, ranchers, doctors, manufacturers, small business owners and families as part of his "120 Stops to Strengthen Rural Kansas" tour. He is concerned about the high costs for fuel and fertilizer as well as the impacts tariffs have on farmers and ranchers. The decision to lift tariffs and import foreign beef had not been announced at the time of that interview. Hamilton is also concerned about the state of rural hospitals. Kansas leads the nation in rural hospitals that are at risk of immediate closure due to the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill last year. Marshall championed his vote for the bill at the time, which made nearly $1 trillion in cuts to Medicaid through 2035. In 2025, United Methodist Health Ministry Fund estimated that Kansas stood to lose nearly $4 billion in federal and state Medicaid funding. The bill also provided a one-time $50 billion distributed over five years in the Rural Health Transformation Program. Kansas received $221 million for the program's first year, far short of the funds needed to offset the Medicaid cuts. In 2024, over 240,000 Kansans were uninsured, a statistically higher rate than the rest of the country. In a statement released after his rural Kansas tour, Marshall said, "We've got a lot to be proud of--from cutting taxes for working families and growing Kansas manufacturing to delivering real resources for our rural hospitals. Will a politics of human decency outweigh party loyalty among voters? Hamilton believes so. At a campaign stop in Greensburg, he recalled one woman who told him, "I want somebody who's going to help me not hate my neighbors anymore," he told the crowd in Emporia. Short-haired, elderly women held down the front row of chairs while Hamilton spoke. They occasionally responded to a question posed by Hamilton, regularly giving a classic Midwestern shake of the head in support or disgust. Among those in the front row was former English teacher, Sharol Cutrell. After Hamilton spoke, she told him she didn't vote for him in the primaries. "I would vote for him today," she told Barn Raiser. "Everything I believe, he's right in line with. And we need somebody like that, somebody neutral, who's for people who don't have as much as we do." Cutrell had concerns about voting for a megachurch pastor in the primary, a sentiment shared by others in the coffee shop that morning. Seeing him in person made her believe he is the right nominee for the challenge. When introducing themselves to Hamilton, many folks gave a brief outline of their family tree, starting with their abolitionist and settler roots in Kansas. A sunflower was incorporated into the design of the banner on the Lyon County Democrats office across the street. In November voters will choose between two fifth-generation Kansans: a MAGA-backed Republican doctor and a Democrat mainline Protestant pastor. #
Peter, we’ve been emailing you about our upcoming FEC deadline on September 30th quite a bit.
The reason we’re doing so is because this is the final, public quarterly FEC report we’ll be legally required to release before the election.
What that means is, this is our last opportunity to put up fundraising numbers that will strike fear into the hearts of the GOP. VoteVets is one of the largest outside spending organizations in politics. When we get into a race, we bring significant resources with us as well as the best advertisements in the game. And when our report gets released, campaign managers and Republican consultants around the country will be watching to see what numbers we post.
Honestly, at this point, the numbers that will really scare them are the number of donations, and the number of unique donors we receive before that deadline. The reason we want them to see that is because it is an unmistakable sign of the strength of this team. We want them to know there is an absolutely massive amount of incoming headed their way, and that it’s coming from us.
So, we’re coming down on our typical ask today. Where we’d typically request $5 or $10, maybe more, today we’re only asking for $2. That’s $2 for VoteVets because just about everyone can afford it, and $2 because we want a ton of people chipping in before that deadline.

A recap of the past year
---
| | [ ](https://clicksp.michaelafortennessee.com/f/a/TiPMyU4oaOtEu-h4c9koYg~~/AAPPABA~/838qcUCBZRcm09aYzEOm8fH3dhxQY5WTndp3_vhW47zpOptjr_T1dK71ehwV93OeyN_wnWc42yLyeGMnAS_EKtz-B-H1Rusqa-giZq4fgSIudhsF6bKDqgtABP2_nV9QsGg1cgcv1YdjFU9YZqMP7PguiLfORRd8rOaW4sdzaGrKet_WrZBxZjRN1p8AvO62cQXzoj7fVp6tMTUJ6JRGnqMnq-RHj_6uGH5hXmWIFPdbxT6QS6tKsUrKIGs1CmIW)

**One year ago today, we launched this campaign to flip TN-02 and serve our neighbors.** I knew then that many people would think this was a waste of time, energy, money - mine and others. That there would be a chorus of naysayers at every turn. What I hoped for, but wasn't assured of, was that there would be much, much larger chorus of people showing up every single day to put in the work for a better future for ourselves and our neighbors. And that's exactly what happened. Over this past year, together we have:
* **Raised over $600,000** \- all from individual, grassroots donors (and 82% from within our district!)
* Had **over 1300 people** sign up to volunteer on this campaign.
* **Invested in East TN** by employing 20 East Tennesseans as well as hired local artists, printers, designers, venues, photographers, videographers, security, translators, and countless others.
* **Held donation drives** for warming centers, community clothing resource centers, teachers and educators, food banks, and more.
* **Reached over 155,000 voters** with texts, postcards, canvassing, friend banking, and phone banking.
* Held **packed events and town halls** in every corner of the district, from Townsend to Cumberland Gap.

And we've made naysayers into believers. Folks who thought it was never going to be possible now believing that _**it just might be**_ , if we all give everything we can. I'm not just talking about money. Now is the time to give a little bit more - time, energy, resources. _**We can do this. **_ **I'll leave you with part of my remarks from one year ago:** "I know a lot of you might be afraid to nurture that tender flame of hope in your bellies, because here in East Tennessee, we are no strangers to disappointment. You might be thinking - I want to believe that change is possible, I want to believe in you, but I just don't know if it is. After Trump was inaugurated, my mentor in DC who had fought through Trump 1.0 shared this advice with all of us in the office. He said: no one is going to tell you what to do. No one is going to give you a guidebook on how to fight back. There is no cavalry coming. **We are the cavalry. ** That is our path to flipping the longest-held Republican district in the country, and ousting a politician who cares more about photo ops and flaming culture war conflicts than serving the people of East Tennessee. In practical terms, we start right now. We meet voters where they are and listen to their concerns and their pain points and what they hope for the future. We hold town halls in every corner of the district and don't shy away from hard conversations with people who disagree with us. We sit down for small listening sessions with workers, with farmers, with veterans, with teachers, with parents, with faith leaders, with immigrants, and with dozens of other groups so that we can have real, honest conversations about what is affecting our community and how we can figure out real solutions - and not just after the election, right now. We build a volunteer army, neighbors talking to neighbors, ready to knock doors, make calls, and spread the word. We grow our movement through each of us reaching out to everyone we know. And we are going to make this campaign joyful: potlucks, concerts, battle of the bands, and block parties. Spaces where politics can feel like hope and connection, not despair and divisiveness. That's how we flip the longest-held Republican district in the country. That's how we build not just a campaign, but a movement that people can't wait to join. _**We put our hope for this region, for our state, for our country - to work. We put hope to work.**_" And friends, that is exactly what we've done. See you out there [on the campaign trail](https://clicksp.michaelafortennessee.com/f/a/_ceRETw9WLwFCE3njoIbgw~~/AAPPABA~/N2xYgIT72WSTqoK3BHwLBt9MkoBiEVzEeLiEqJLTpzcxizXz7QU6sva_OaXCoj6VDmjjTNz0ZixPMrR1MQvVi6LypJ_v7Kb7_o11MTh_0DeLlo96lxXD3rI9dCHmCwvEIFrLL4l2Y-uRugKTRUCE6bsjb6seXVVPu5LZjUtDNWDXc5AVm7mdl2puX4Rz1L1OEPIjiAzLlVV5W-hF762ZWl1WLDaVjKR-1XFS0VUJevJ1URc5tekgYeAWH2jscPV185N-x0BJRiAVRM7h0CYbFnrsjDWulKQ_g3_R0NmUPSE~) over the next five weeks. In gratitude and solidarity, Michaela _P.S. See you at the[anniversary canvass today](https://clicksp.michaelafortennessee.com/f/a/bt_X3uYI6iRSPY6hrStw6Q~~/AAPPABA~/rWg3Zf1uC5EjhxC-NZGskpHeCbQlL-60qpr2rmftQzEQpchWylzJ7ePC8ejjxyUXaBqm6llhqtz7mUh2Zo0zhB--wq2ynvleGLDZ5fuxYsQoi2V8sUY51WNT23FS8fUPpihD43RAdhF4HUl4Rj5Dmf6H30VC9x2Pvy3HglTTIoLPgC2oESYEvaPkJWPYExY5638ACeqWMrla6Byjt_q6kOCK-6nkD7UW2DkDftHTBwPZgjrznPtHK15y_kyayoAHpXDf3gqyibz97YVf-ylPYyvfPf_zgSXyREtd4LfYiPQ~) at 1 p.m. at Urban Wilderness Gateway park in South Knoxville?_

clean_body: A recap of the past year | | One year ago today, we launched this campaign to flip TN-02 and serve our neighbors. I knew then that many people would think this was a waste of time, energy, money - mine and others. That there would be a chorus of naysayers at every turn. What I hoped for, but wasn't assured of, was that there would be much, much larger chorus of people showing up every single day to put in the work for a better future for ourselves and our neighbors. And that's exactly what happened. Over this past year, together we have: Raised over $600,000 \- all from individual, grassroots donors (and 82% from within our district!) Had over 1300 people sign up to volunteer on this campaign. Invested in East TN by employing 20 East Tennesseans as well as hired local artists, printers, designers, venues, photographers, videographers, security, translators, and countless others. Held donation drives for warming centers, community clothing resource centers, teachers and educators, food banks, and more. Reached over 155,000 voters with texts, postcards, canvassing, friend banking, and phone banking. Held packed events and town halls in every corner of the district, from Townsend to Cumberland Gap. And we've made naysayers into believers. Folks who thought it was never going to be possible now believing that it just might be , if we all give everything we can. I'm not just talking about money. Now is the time to give a little bit more - time, energy, resources. We can do this. I'll leave you with part of my remarks from one year ago: "I know a lot of you might be afraid to nurture that tender flame of hope in your bellies, because here in East Tennessee, we are no strangers to disappointment. You might be thinking - I want to believe that change is possible, I want to believe in you, but I just don't know if it is. After Trump was inaugurated, my mentor in DC who had fought through Trump 1.0 shared this advice with all of us in the office. He said: no one is going to tell you what to do. No one is going to give you a guidebook on how to fight back. There is no cavalry coming. We are the cavalry. That is our path to flipping the longest-held Republican district in the country, and ousting a politician who cares more about photo ops and flaming culture war conflicts than serving the people of East Tennessee. In practical terms, we start right now. We meet voters where they are and listen to their concerns and their pain points and what they hope for the future. We hold town halls in every corner of the district and don't shy away from hard conversations with people who disagree with us. We sit down for small listening sessions with workers, with farmers, with veterans, with teachers, with parents, with faith leaders, with immigrants, and with dozens of other groups so that we can have real, honest conversations about what is affecting our community and how we can figure out real solutions - and not just after the election, right now. We build a volunteer army, neighbors talking to neighbors, ready to knock doors, make calls, and spread the word. We grow our movement through each of us reaching out to everyone we know. And we are going to make this campaign joyful: potlucks, concerts, battle of the bands, and block parties. Spaces where politics can feel like hope and connection, not despair and divisiveness. That's how we flip the longest-held Republican district in the country. That's how we build not just a campaign, but a movement that people can't wait to join. We put our hope for this region, for our state, for our country - to work. We put hope to work." And friends, that is exactly what we've done. See you out there ~ over the next five weeks. In gratitude and solidarity, Michaela P.S. See you at the~ at 1 p.m. at Urban Wilderness Gateway park in South Knoxville? | We have just over five weeks left to go. | | | Oregon didn't just adopt vote-by-mail. We INVENTED it. **So when President Trump signs an executive order restricting mail-in ballots, understand what that means: ** No state has more on the line than Oregon. This order isn't aimed at some abstract "voting system." **It targets how every single Oregonian votes.** Here's what Trump’s USPS order does. It orders the Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters on a federal list — a list built by THIS administration. Their postmaster already said the quiet part out loud: states that don't hand over their voter data likely won't have mail ballots delivered at all. Now here's what I know. **I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. We have taken this administration to court — over their demand for your voter data, and over their first election order. We won/** _**They still are not stopping. **_ **The Constitution hasn't changed**. States run elections. Not presidents. Not postmasters. And this November, Oregon will run the same safe, fair, accurate vote-by-mail election we've run for 25 years — and I will use every power of this office to make sure of it. **[But fighting them in court is only one way to defend our elections. We must have the resources to communicate about what’s at stake — every lawsuit, every rule change, every attempt to rewrite how Oregon votes. That’s why I’m using my campaign to help travel around the state and talk directly to voters too.
