name: Chris Pappas
subject: Let me explain why this week’s deadline is so important
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9161%2E582294%2EgkWBBr ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9161%2E582294%2EgkWBBr ]Chris Pappas for Senate

This Wednesday’s FEC end-of-quarter deadline is the most important of the
entire campaign. Let me explain.

On September 30th at midnight, we face our final end-of-quarter deadline
before Election Day. Our campaign set a $1 million fundraising goal to
keep us on track for the final stretch, and here’s why:

📊 Republican John Sununu is surging ahead in polls.

📡 National Republicans are outspending us 3-to-1 on the airwaves.

🗳️ Every dollar that we raise today determines what we can budget for the
final 37 days until Election Day.

If we fall short now, we risk letting Republicans not only flip this seat
but lock up the Senate majority for a generation.

Granite Staters’ hard-earned Social Security. Lowering the cost of
healthcare. Reproductive rights.

That’s what’s on the line.

We can protect these priorities by beating Sununu in November. But only if
we raise the resources we need to compete.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260927_2.lQJMJ0&refcode=em20260927-2&t=1003&akid=9161%2E582294%2EgkWBBr ]I’m
directly asking you: Will you chip in $5 to help us reach
our end-of-quarter goal of $1 million and keep this seat from falling into
Republican hands?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260927_2.lQJMJ0&amount=5&refcode=em20260927-2&t=1022&akid=9161%2E582294%2EgkWBBr ]Donate $5 »

This $1 million goal isn’t arbitrary — it’s what we need to compete and
win over the next five weeks. If you’re able to help us reach it today, it
would be a massive help to everything we’re trying to accomplish. [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260927_2.lQJMJ0&refcode=em20260927-2&t=1023&akid=9161%2E582294%2EgkWBBr ]I
would be very grateful for your $5 contribution.

Thank you,

Chris

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

Regular readers of _Navigating Uncertainty_ know that I have long felt that global multilateral institutions such as the United Nations are ineffective and, in many cases, work against the interests of their member institutions. While the concept of global governance to coordinate global responses for global challenges makes intuitive sense, it simply hasn't worked.
## [Global Multilateralism Is Dead](https://substack.com/redirect/f6e2bd4a-1d4f-4686-989d-ff5ec207f7e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

[Conventional wisdom and Western policies long believed that an economically prosperous China would ultimately become more democratic. For better or worse, the opposite has happened. China is today far more autocratic than at any point in modern history, something the West, in its misguided approach to embracing China, has](https://substack.com/redirect/f6e2bd4a-1d4f-4686-989d-ff5ec207f7e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

## [Global Multilateralism Remains Dead](https://substack.com/redirect/4417efc1-7e0b-4f71-b633-71ee3322f0ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| September 27, 2025
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4417efc1-7e0b-4f71-b633-71ee3322f0ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Two years ago I wrote an article entitled, "Global Multilateralism is Dead." The piece generated a lot of feedback, most of which was negative. Former colleagues from academia reached out to suggest my views were not helpful and global organizations stopped inviting me to speak at their gatherings. But the years since I penned the piece have delivered p...](https://substack.com/redirect/4417efc1-7e0b-4f71-b633-71ee3322f0ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/4417efc1-7e0b-4f71-b633-71ee3322f0ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Global multilateralism has lost all credibility. Do we really think the UN Security Council is useful when one of its members is the aggressor in a war that's killed millions? Or what about the World Health Organization, which refused to investigate the origins of COVID, the world's biggest public health challenge in a century? Surely we can't have faith in the World Trade Organization if it doesn't address state-sponsored intellectual property theft?
Just this week, US President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei delivered comments at the United Nations General Assembly describing the death of global multilateralism. Trump's tariffs, tirades against NATO, pullback from Europe, refocusing of US attention on the Western Hemisphere, and ~~willingness~~ preference for unilateral action have delivered the "post-WWII international order" body blow after body blow. And if you doubt this trend or Trump's intentions, listen to his blunt and defiant speech before the United Nations last week (link below).
[](https://substack.com/redirect/a47c2294-35ac-4f35-aeae-c4604d1751b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Trump took aim at multilateralism and global institutions. He called the International Criminal Court "full of evil people" with no jurisdiction over the United States and called on nations to withdraw from it. He attacked the UN Human Rights Council for focusing on the US while overlooking abuses elsewhere. He made clear that the United States would not subordinate its sovereignty to multilateral groups, and challenged other nations to follow suit.
Remarkably, Trump was not even the most vocal critic of the UN to speak at the UN during the general assembly. Argentina's Javier Milei took the same podium and made the American president sound like a polished career diplomat. The UN, Milei noted, was a "useless organization" that "only serves to feed a caste of parasites." The bodies charged with guaranteeing collective security and human rights, he argued, failed at the task and allowed chaos, violence, and international terrorism to flourish, while the self-appointed defenders of human rights sheltered dictatorships and regimes that brutalize women.
Milei's speech was stunning, and it's worth 20 minutes of your time (link below). He described the United Nations as a "bureaucratic leviathan devoted to deciding how the peoples of the world and their citizens should live" and thereby producing a curious hybrid of anarchy and tyranny. He suggested it was impotent toward those who break the most basic rules, and exerted Orwellian control over the liberal democracies that actually follow them.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/7ff8316a-1f0b-43f5-ad1a-2c36b0930010?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But the most important line in Milei's speech was an eloquent caveat. Argentina, he said, will keep participating in multilateral forums in good faith but urged listeners to not "confuse cooperation with subordination." The objection isn't to nations working together. It's a rejection of a permanent class of officials nobody elected claiming authority over people who never consented to it, and to "cooperation" that has quietly hardened into a sense of "obligation" in conflict with sovereignty.
Ironically, the speeches were a sideshow. The real story was what happened in the hallways. On the sidelines of the General Assembly, Trump signed a _bilateral_ security agreement with Denmark and Greenland. He met with Venezuela's acting president and announced a _bilateral_ oil deal. He held one-on-one meetings with the leaders of Japan, Ukraine, and the GCC nations. The United Nations General Assembly has become a venue in which _bilateral_ deals get done...multilateral speech is theater, the bilateral meetings are the real work.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/750b3635-6590-4bee-aa0a-d8f0527d29aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Multilateralism has been withering for some time. The Abraham Accords were _bilateral_. The Iran war wasn't authorized by the UN. Pakistan's mediation between the US and Iran is _bilateral_. China's Belt and Road Initiative is a web of _bilateral_ deals. The European Union is struggling to hold together as Hungary and Poland resist Brussels on everything from migration to the rule of law. Everywhere you look, nationalism is resurgent and nation states are asserting their sovereignty.
So what replaces multilateralism? It's not chaos. It's transactional bilateralism, adorned in the language of national interest. Countries aren't withdrawing from the international order because they're isolationist. They're withdrawing because these institutions no longer serve their interests, and in many cases, actively work against them. Milei and Trump are the loudest voices, but there's a chorus of other leaders joining them. India's Modi, China's Xi, Turkey's Erdogan, and Italy's Meloni. are all prioritizing bilateral arrangements over multilateral commitments. The world is increasingly betting that sovereignty trumps solidarity.
The question, of course, is whether deal-by-deal arrangements can adequately address challenges that cross borders and impact the entire planet: climate change, pandemics, nuclear proliferation, the acceleration of AI, transnational terrorism and crime, and the regulation of the global commons. These problems don't respect borders. They require coordination at scale. The problem is the institutions designed to provide that coordination don't work.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/3ddbe001-8155-410a-81f1-77b3a7ea340f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It's worth remembering, though, that we have run this experiment before -- and that the first attempt failed far more spectacularly. The League of Nations was born in 1920 out of Woodrow Wilson's conviction that collective security could replace the balance of power, and the US Senate promptly refused to join the institution its own president had designed. What followed was fifteen years of escalating humiliation. Japan invaded Manchuria in 1931 and, when the League objected, simply walked out. Germany withdrew in 1933. Italy invaded Abyssinia in 1935, and the sanctions the League imposed were so carefully calibrated to avoid offending Rome that they excluded oil. The Soviet Union was expelled in 1939 for invading Finland, by which point there was scarcely anything left to be expelled from. Nor was the League an isolated failure. The Kellogg-Briand Pact of 1928, signed by more than sixty nations, outlawed war as an instrument of national policy exactly eleven years before the deadliest war in human history.
**The lesson is that multilateral institutions are not natural in a world defined by nation states. They are brief, fragile, and conditional, and they last precisely as long as their most powerful members find them useful ...and not one day longer.**
In 1975, Chevy Chase opened Saturday Night Live's Weekend Update with a running gag that became the show's first viral catchphrase. Every week, with mock seriousness, he would announce: "This just in: Generalissimo Francisco Franco is still dead."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/93889179-c647-4ae6-a9f6-eeb13b1584d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And so, at the risk of stealing his bit, I will say once again...**this just in: multilateralism is still dead.** Let it rest in peace. But let's be honest about the cause of death: not populism, but a lack of legitimacy the institutions never took seriously.
Abraham Lincoln set the standard at Gettysburg in a set of words that captured the essence of legitimacy in governance: "government of the people, by the people, for the people." Global multilateralism failed to incorporate this logic, instead building institutions of the elites, by the elites, and for the elites, staffed by people no voter chose and no voter can remove. As Milei noted, sovereign nations can still cooperate. They do it every day, and it has a name: _diplomacy_. But citizens of the world have spoken clearly over hundreds of years. They will only be governed by leaders they can fire. That clause is missing from every charter ever drafted, and until someone writes it in, multilateralism will keep dying -- over and over, in exactly the same way.

This past Friday, my former congressional colleague, Steve Stivers, and I published a new piece in the _Washington Examiner_ making the bipartisan case for permitting reform.
That may not sound like the most exciting topic, but it is one of the most fundamental. If we want to lower energy costs, build more housing, expand American manufacturing, modernize our infrastructure, and compete in AI, we have to get much better at actually building things.
You can read a preview below and read the full piece in the _[Washington Examiner](https://substack.com/redirect/87c75196-00af-4824-b9a4-9bd85e332499?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ here.
> Throughout **[American history](https://substack.com/redirect/dac02fcd-bd00-486b-ab56-d8e970973af2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , there have been moments when building on an enormous scale has been a national necessity. Think of how the New Deal brought electricity to **[rural communities](https://substack.com/redirect/bd11b8f1-df48-46fa-bce0-d3a8cb6da4e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , or how two decades later, Dwight Eisenhower launched the Interstate Highway System, one of the largest public-works projects in our nation's history.
> We are entering another such moment for infrastructure in this country. After decades of relatively flat electricity demand, the United States is suddenly asking much more of its physical **[economy](https://substack.com/redirect/f884377f-88de-45d2-a86b-8e82f68d6f23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. We need more housing in the places where people most want to live, more power for factories and businesses, and a stronger industrial base capable of supplying our military in an increasingly dangerous world. Competition with China raises the stakes further -- the race for leadership in artificial intelligence requires enormous amounts of electricity and computing capacity, as well as the infrastructure to support both.
Continue reading at the _[Washington Examiner](https://substack.com/redirect/87c75196-00af-4824-b9a4-9bd85e332499?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[.](https://substack.com/redirect/87c75196-00af-4824-b9a4-9bd85e332499?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

subject: Sleeping on NC = snatching defeat from the jaws of victory
body:
Roy can’t overcome the full force of the GOP’s dark-money machine on his own
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1445&source=&t=1&akid=3876%2E124072%2EO-pzBb) | | | |

[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1445&amount=5&t=8&akid=3876%2E124072%2EO-pzBb)
Now looky here, Peter:
**Democrats have a snowball’s chance in hell of retaking the U.S. Senate majority this fall without flipping North Carolina’s red seat blue.**
Ain’t nobody’s done that since 2008, and right now, the GOP is flooding _beaucoup bucks_ into NC to keep it that way. That’s ‘cause having a proven winner like two-term former Governor Roy Cooper as the Democratic nominee is our best chance of flipping _any_ of the four seats we need.
Roy can’t overcome the full force of the GOP’s dark-money machine on his own, [**_so if you’re my kind of Democrat – the kind who believes our #1 mission is to take back the Senate from Trump’s far-right flunkies – then I’mma need you to get off your derrière and pitch in $5 or more to his grassroots campaign ASAP._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1445&amount=5&t=9&akid=3876%2E124072%2EO-pzBb)
Now you'll have to pardon my French, but I'm scared sh*tless Democrats just don't get how bad we need to fight for North Carolina this year.
Every election since 2008, the polls and expert ratings had us convinced NC was going our way ... only for some milquetoast Republican jack*ss to beat us by a few points on Election Day.
And believe me: **The jack*ss Roy’s up against this November has _a lot_ going his way.**
His GOP opponent Michael Whatley is the former chair of the RNC, so big-time Republicans like the President and my evil twin Stephen Miller are putting their thumbs on the scales in his favor.
On top of that, their super PACs are spending over _$100 million_ so far on baseless attack ads against Roy – **and now, a recent poll shows his slim lead SHRINKING. This race is officially a statistically tied ballgame.**
Without the grassroots resources to surge ahead and reach every last voter between the Outer Banks and the Smokies, Roy could lose this race – and Democrats can say goodbye to flipping the Senate!!!
[**_If you want to stop that from happening, then PLEASE, Peter, before midnight, rush $5 or anything you can spare – _toot sweet_ – to help Roy reach his FEC end-of-quarter goal to fight back and win in North Carolina. The future of our country depends on it._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1445&amount=5&t=10&akid=3876%2E124072%2EO-pzBb)

It’s John James. First, thank you for opening this message. I know your time is limited, so I’ll get to the point quickly: I need a fully funded war chest to win my race for Governor -and that means asking for your help. Right now, the Left and the Democrat Establishment are going ballistic at the thought of someone like me becoming for Governor. 👉 Trump-Endorsed 👉Iraq Army War Veteran 👉Christian Conservative Patriot, the Radical Left doesn’t scare me. But you know what does? Losing our country to the woke, socialist, trans-supporting progressives that want to burn every last American flag to ashes. Right now, only a MASSIVE cash advantage can put me over the top and keep the America First agenda alive and thriving. So today, I’m only asking for $1. $1 from EVERY patriot like you—the truckers, teachers, waitresses, cops, firefighters, and everyone else working night and day just to make ends meet—could save my campaign. Every dollar fuels our movement, whether it’s spreading new yard signs across the state or buying pizza and water for my grassroots volunteers. I promise, this is the last time I’ll ask you,Patriot: As a veteran, a Christian, a father, and the best MAGA fighter you have in Congress, please: Time is running out.
